sourceName: NVIDIA, UC Berkeley, Stanford and CMU researchers
title: CaP-X gives coding agents a physical exam in robot control
friendlyTitle: A new test measures how well AI can control robots
summary: CaP-X is an open framework for testing language-model agents that write executable robot-control code across more than 100 manipulation tasks. Its published results put the strongest tested frontier model at 32.3% average success against an 88.5% human baseline, while post-training a 7B coding model substantially improved selected simulation and real-robot tasks.
friendlySummary: CaP-X asks AI models to write code for more than 100 robot tasks. The best tested model completed far fewer tasks than people, showing both real progress and a large gap.
whyItMatters: The benchmark makes progress in embodied AI measurable instead of relying on impressive demonstrations. It also suggests a practical architecture: let language models plan at a higher level while specialized control systems handle precise physical movement.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Reliable tests help teams see what robot agents can really do. The results also show that AI still needs careful limits and specialist control systems around physical work.
